text:
mira: heads-up — flipping on FP8 KV cache for mistral-8b in canary cluster caused p99 token latency to jump ~18% on long-context workloads. saw this after last night's rollout. attaching quick profiler dump below.

sahil: do you have a repro script or exact pool name? is this only mistral or mixtral too?

mira: repro command: `./run_infer --model mistral-8b --pool canary-mistral-fp8 --seq 2048 --batch 1 --kv-cache enabled` — also observed on mixtral-8x when sequence > 1024. short seqs (<256) are fine.

mira: profiler snippet:
```
[timeline]
0.000 - request enqueue
0.005 - kernel_select: matmul_fp8_native (fast)
0.013 - kernel_dispatch_wait: 8ms
0.021 - kv_copy_cpu: 12ms  <-- large blowup vs fp16
0.033 - kv_merge_gpu: 1.5ms
0.036 - total_token_ms: 36ms (prev 30ms)
memory: kv_cache -35% (gpu), cpu_copy +12%
```

ana: interesting. NV kernel is faster but we might be hitting an extra host<->device memcpy for fp8-packed KV. could be our packing/unpacking routine runs on CPU for large prefixes.

chris: do we have a trace that shows where the memcpy is invoked? can the kernel accept the packed layout directly? if not, kernel selection should fallback to a layout-compatible matmul kernel.

mira: trace attached in slack file (small). it shows `kv_pack_to_fp8()` called on CPU path when prefix_len > 512. suspect heuristic threshold wrong in batching code.

sahil: batching heuristics could amplify this: if average batch size drops (we saw avg 4 -> 2) then amortization of pack cost is worse. what are batching windows and flush triggers in canary config?

mira: canary config:
```
batch.window_ms = 12
batch.max_tokens = 2048
kv.precision = fp8
kv.fallback_precision = fp16
kv.eviction_policy = lru_by_age
```

ana: proposal: precision-tiering + tiered eviction. rules:
- keep recent prefixes in fp8 packed GPU memory (fast, dense)
- promote long-lived but infrequently accessed prefixes to fp16 halves on GPU or quantized on host
- avoid CPU repack on critical path: prepack in async worker before request dispatch
- if batch_size < 3 and seq_len > 512 -> force fp16 kernel to avoid cpu pack overhead

ana: config sketch (pseudocode):
```
kv.tiering.enabled = true
kv.tiering.hot_threshold = 3   # accesses/frame
kv.tiering.prepack_async = true
kv.routing.precision_hint = { short_seq: fp8, long_seq: fp16 }
kv.eviction.strategy = size_aware_lru
```

chris: also double-check RoPE scaling interactions for Qwen variants — we had earlier misaligned head offsets when we changed kernel layout, leading to extra matmul reshapes. could be showing up only on certain head_kv dims (e.g., 64 vs 80). Add a head/kv-dim compatibility check in kernel selector.

mira: good call. the failing mixtral run was with head_kv=64 and rope.scale=1.06. when I forced kernel to `matmul_fp16_aligned` p99 drops back to baseline. so kernel selector needs a guard on (precision, head_kv, rope_scale) tuple.

perf-bot: PERF ALERT: canary-mistral-fp8 p99 tokens increased 17.9% vs baseline in last 3 deploys — ticket #PF-4821 created.

sahil: plan: revert fp8 default for long prefixes immediately, keep fp8 for short prefix fast-path. create a canary with `prepack_async=true` and `batch.window_ms=8` for further tests. I'll own an A/B run.

ana: I'll file perf PR to add tiering knobs + kernel compatibility checks. also add unit test to verify no CPU pack on request-critical path.

mira: thanks. I'll attach the full profiler and sample requests to PF-4821. assign @sahil for rollback run, @ana for PR. :thumbsup:

chris: one more — add a perf counter for `kv_cpu_pack_ms` and `kv_async_prepack_hits` so we can gate rollouts by those metrics.

mira: adding to ticket. closing this thread once A/B is running.
